results.text: BREAKOUT requires Close above Prior20High and ADX14 at least 18, after high-volatility rejection. This breakout classification is evaluated before the TREND classification and permits the BREAKOUT strategy.

results.title: Materiality of routine penalties and regulatory notices
results.text: A monetary penalty, fine, tax or duty demand, late fee or similar routine regulatory notice is an adverse event only when the cited sources show at least one of the following: the amount is significant relative to the issuer's reported profit, revenue or net worth in the cited financial filing; it restricts operations, licences, management, listing or the ability to do business; it alleges fraud or misconduct; or the issuer itself reports a material impact. The comparison uses the issuer's own reported figures, never a fixed rupee threshold. A notice that meets none of these conditions is recorded in limitations with its document cited, leaves event_risks empty, permits NO_MATERIAL_ADVERSE_FOUND when the adverse-disclosure scan is ready, does not block an entry and does not force an exit in a holding review. If the amount or its scale cannot be read, the event risk is UNKNOWN and blocks entry. Reason: large issuers disclose small penalties almost every month under Regulation 30; treating each one as adverse made C2 refuse every entry in such stocks, which is abstention by rule and not evidence review. This rule changes classification only; it never changes sizing, stops or other code-owned risk limits.

results.title: Daily-bar SMC strategy definition
results.text: SMC is a code-defined daily-bar price-action approximation, not proof of institutional activity. Regular first entries require a low below the prior 20 completed lows with close back above that level; within ten bars a later bullish displacement close exceeds the five-bar pre-sweep high with body at least 0.5 ATR; the last preceding bearish candle defines an order block from its low to open. Within ten further bars a later candle overlaps the zone and closes bullish above its upper bound. A close below its low invalidates the setup. No same-sweep/BOS-bar entry, future-confirmed pivots or required FVG. A qualifying close fills at a later eligible open only after evidence and code/risk checks. Normal exits use a configurable net profit target (C1 default 4%), protective stops, optionally enabled trailing, and cited adverse C1 EXIT. No EMA/RSI signal exit or forced terminal sale applies to SMC. These prototype parameters are not optimized or proven profitable. A stopped-position recovery is a separate code-owned variant under POL-75; it never substitutes price recovery for fresh company evidence.

results.title: Entry gap invalidates a stop
results.text: The initial protective stop is fixed from signal-time evidence before the entry fills. If the next eligible open makes that stop invalid or violates sizing constraints, the engine rejects the queued BUY. After a historical fill, an explicitly enabled trailing stop may only rise at a completed close: max(previous stop, highest completed close since entry minus the configured multiple of entry-signal ATR14). The ATR distance stays fixed; a raised stop applies from the next session and cannot be tested against the earlier low of the same bar. The LLM cannot lower or veto this coded protective exit. Historical portfolios may also exit at the configured take-profit percentage, default eight percent NET of modeled entry and exit fees with adverse slippage in execution. Opening gaps are processed before intraday triggers. If an intraday daily bar touches both stop and target without a known order, use the stop first. Stops, targets and code exits cannot be vetoed by an LLM. No final-period liquidation is forced.

results.title: Daily turnover filter
results.text: Daily screening requires a mean Close times Volume of at least ten million rupees over 20 sessions, equivalent to one crore rupees per day. This project liquidity screen is distinct from official index eligibility criteria. A candidate must also satisfy readiness, volatility, entry, cash and capacity checks.

results.title: RSI selection strength
results.text: For an RSI_REVERSION candidate, the intermediate strength is the value of (42 minus RSI14) divided by 22, clipped between zero and one. This measures depth relative to the project entry threshold after eligibility screening. It does not change the stop, cash or planned-risk controls.
